translation_notes: initNs={'odml': ..., 'rdf': RDF, 'rdfs': RDFS} becomes three @prefix declarations, none of them interpolated in the query body: the site is pure prefix binding, no initBindings term. This is the 'prologue herite des @prefix' half of the bind_initbindings row, not the term-interpolation half.

ODML_NS is a plain string built at run time in the source repo (imported from odml.tools.rdf_converter), so the odml: prefix uses a formatted IRI (f<{ODML_NS}>) rather than a literal <...> -- declarations.md documents this exact case (a computed prefix IRI).

The region only prepares the query (prepareQuery / s{ }); it is never iterated where it is written. The repository consumes it on the next line, `for row in graph.query(q): print(row.d, row.s)`, and that call is kept unchanged: ldpy 0.7.1 accepts the s{ } value in graph.query(). The driver runs that call on both sides, compares (row.d, row.s) and the projected variables of SELECT *, reads the translated q also through the call suffix (q(g).execute(), which must give the same rows), and probes that graph.query(q) on the s{ } value succeeds (verdict key graph_query_on_island).

The site uses initNs only (-> @prefix), no initBindings, so it exercises the prologue half of the bind_initbindings row, not the term-interpolation half. Fixture: two matching sections and three neighbours that must not match (non-Document parent, child not typed Section, case-different hasType), plus a document with no matching section. Mutants killed: dropping either rdf:type pattern, changing the hasType literal, hasSection replaced by hasType, SELECT ?s instead of SELECT *.
